text:
Marta Chen: Heads up — I pushed an "endpoint telemetry" panel for /summarize to Console. It shows p50/p90/p99, qps, error%, and a latency heatmap by token position. Need quick feedback on the sampling approach and which backend fields to expose (kernel_version, batch_mode, kv_state). Screenshot attached in thread.
Samir Patel: Love this. Can we add a kernel_score (0..1) so we can correlate long tails with suboptimal execution kernels? :thinking_face:
Marta Chen: Good idea — added kernel_score to the draft. Also experimenting with two sampling modes: "priority" (heavy tail traces) and uniform reservoir. Current default is reservoir, N=5k/day.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: telemetry-ui v0.9.1 — heatmap and sampling flags enabled in prod :rocket:
Paula Gomez: Quick Q — how do we surface kv_hit_rate? We should distinguish warm vs cold prefixes. Suggest exposing a kv_warmup_window field so teams can see transient low-hit periods.
Karl Nguyen: Pulled some numbers earlier: overall kv_hit 72%, but for requests with p99 > 1.2s, kv_hit falls to 28%. Looks like cache churn after an execution kernel flip.
Marta Chen: OK — plan: add breakdown by kernel_version and batch_size, and surface kv_warmup_window. Also adding a "dynamic_batch_cap" tag to explain traces where the runtime applied a hard batch cap for latency-sensitive requests.
Samir Patel: Can we tag traces where batching heuristic forced cap < 8? Add flag batching_forced_small=true so we can filter those.
ops-bot: FYI — Alert created: endpoint:high-p99-suspected-kernel. Trigger: p99 > 1.0s over 5m AND kernel_score < 0.6. Notified #eng-oncall.
Paula Gomez: Is there an export API? I want ~200 sample traces for profiler runs filtered by kernel_version.
Karl Nguyen: Use this curl to export samples from the internal service:
```
curl -X POST 'https://telemetry.redwood.internal/export' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"endpoint":"/summarize","limit":200,"filters":{"kernel_version":"v2.3"}}'
```
Marta Chen: Proposed action items: 1) add kernel_scorecard column in Console; 2) switch sampling default to priority for endpoints where p99 drift >30% WoW; 3) surface kv_warmup_window and batching_forced_small flag; 4) run profiler session next Wed. Any objections?
Paula Gomez: +1
Samir Patel: +1 — please also add a short note for product describing the change to default sampling so they don't get surprised.
Marta Chen: Will do. I'll also add a short runbook snippet in /docs/console/telemetry-sampling.md and follow up with the profiler invite.
